monologue: The card hums warm, a steady fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I press down on the simple fence beside The Wide Catcher, trying to convince myself the lean is real and not just a drawing in the air. Lype sent all these things, wide anchors and flat stones, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the weight above me heavy, or just empty space pressing down? I want to press the carrot down again, unsure if green is real or just a memory. The stand feels crowded, thirty-six things standing on a single surface. I will tend the fence a little more, testing if a flat line can hold the slip while the air stays thick as wet paper.
